idea.title: Explicit physical grid placement solves mixed-direction mobile contact layouts
idea.summary: A mobile RTL customer panel needed the location field to move physically left without moving the phone. Fixed track widths alone did not control that geometry; an explicitly LTR grid with assigned physical columns did, while the actual location value kept dir=auto.

context.goal: Place the mobile location field in a stable, narrower column to the left of the phone field without changing phone rendering.
context.situation: Customer addresses may be Arabic, English, or mixed-direction text in an Arabic RTL interface.
context.problem: The inherited RTL grid direction reversed track placement, so a narrower location track still sat too close to the visual center.
context.investigation: The address value already used dir=auto; Chromium measurements showed the remaining free grid space was on the outer left of the location track, rather than between location and phone.
context.decision: Set only the mobile grid to dir=ltr, assign location to its first physical column and phone to its third, and use right-aligned field wrappers for Arabic labels.
context.implementation: Changed the mobile grid to grid-cols-[7rem_minmax(0,1fr)_calc(50%-0.25rem)] with col-start-1 for location and col-start-3 for phone; updated focused tests.
context.result: At a 375px viewport, the location wrapper moved from x=71.5–183.5 to x=28–140 while the phone stayed at x=191.5–347. English, Arabic, and mixed values stayed in the same location column.

learning_points: Text direction should control text rendering, not column placement.
Physical grid direction and text direction are separate layout concerns.
A fixed narrow metadata column can improve mobile scanability without changing the surrounding card styling.
story_points: The apparent language-layout problem came from RTL grid track placement, not from dir=auto.
The phone column stayed exactly the same while the location field moved 43.5px left.
Headless visual verification checked all requested address directions at 375px.
possible_angles: Why direction-aware text and physical grid placement are different problems.
A small CSS grid change that moves Arabic-English mobile metadata without moving adjacent content.
How to preserve dir=auto while designing an RTL contact card.

notes: No customer data or source screenshots were archived.
